paper_sections.title: History of withdrawal modulates drug- and food-cue reactivity in cocaine dependent participants
Neural reactivity to DRUG and FOOD videos
Moderating role of drug use history and psychopathic traits

description.value: The study examined whether a history of DSM-IV-TR cocaine withdrawal modulates neural drug-versus-food cue reactivity in cocaine-dependent participants, and whether drug-use history and psychopathic traits moderate these biases.

design.value: Secondary analyses of an existing sample compared cocaine-dependent participants with and without a history of withdrawal and non-dependent controls during an fMRI cue-reactivity task.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM Disorders (SCID-IV)

description.value: Administered to assess all psychiatric disorders, including the presence of lifetime cocaine dependence disorder.

name.value: DSM-IV-TR criteria for cocaine withdrawal

description.value: Participants were asked about withdrawal symptoms after cutting down or stopping cocaine and use of cocaine or another drug to prevent withdrawal symptoms; those answering yes were assessed for dysphoric mood and withdrawal symptoms.

name.value: Addiction Severity Index-Expanded

description.value: A modified version was used to calculate a Major Drug Use composite score by summating the number of years of regular use of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, and other amphetamine/opiates.

name.value: Timeline Follow-Back

description.value: Used to collect detailed information regarding cocaine use over the 90 days prior to the scanning session.

name.value: Psychopathy Checklist-Revised (PCL-R)

description.value: A semi-structured clinical assessment consisting of 20 items rated 0–2, with total scores ranging from 0 to 40.

name.value: Wechsler abbreviated scale of intelligence (WASI)

description.value: The two-subset WASI was used to obtain full-scale IQ estimates.

VideoType
Major Drug Use (MDU)

source_definition.value: The number of years of regular use of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, and other amphetamine/opiates.

name.value: PCL-R scores

source_definition.value: Psychopathic traits assessed using the Psychopathy Checklist-Revised.

name.value: age
WD

description.value: Cocaine-dependent participants who showed DSM-IV-derived evidence of lifetime withdrawal.

exclusion_criteria.value: Evidence of lifetime psychotic disorder, major depressive disorder in the last 6 months, or current use of antipsychotic medication

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM Disorders (SCID-IV)

clinical_characteristics.value: Mean PCL-R score across the whole sample was 18.48 (SD = 7.14, range = 4–34); mean MDU score was 7.13 years (SD = 7.97, range = 0–33).

medication_status.value: Current use of antipsychotic medication was grounds for exclusion.

name.value: N-WD

description.value: Cocaine-dependent participants who did not confirm DSM-IV-derived withdrawal criteria or who responded no to both parent withdrawal questions.

exclusion_criteria.value: Evidence of lifetime psychotic disorder, major depressive disorder in the last 6 months, or current use of antipsychotic medication

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM Disorders (SCID-IV)

name.value: ND

description.value: Participants who did not meet DSM-IV-TR criteria for dependence.

exclusion_criteria.value: Evidence of lifetime psychotic disorder, major depressive disorder in the last 6 months, or current use of antipsychotic medication

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM Disorders (SCID-IV)

task_description.value: Participants viewed videos related to the creation/administration of either drugs or food.

design_type.value: Two identical runs; event-related video presentation with inter-trial jitter

stimuli.value: 29 videos: 15 depicted individuals preparing or using cocaine and 14 depicted individuals preparing or eating food; video duration was approximately 10,000–14,000 ms.

description.value: Participants performed the cue-reactivity paradigm within a 3T Siemens TrioTim MRI scanner.

model_settings.value: The design matrix modeled the hemodynamic response during FOOD and DRUG videos and included six movement parameters: x, y, z, pitch, yaw, and roll.

The model included Group (WD, N-WD, ND), VideoType (DRUG, FOOD), and the Group*VideoType interaction. Whole-brain results were threshold at 0.001 uncorrected with an extended cluster threshold of 102 voxels, equivalent to p < .05 FWE. Small-volume corrected search spheres were 10 mm for cortical regions and 6 mm for subcortical regions.

Among dependent participants, Group (WD or N-WD), PCL-R scores, and MDU scores were entered as separate first-level regressors; Group*PCL-R, Group*MDU, and PCL-R*MDU were entered as second-level regressors; and the three-way interaction was entered as a third-level regressor. Models were run with and without age.
